newsitem.title: USA: Comsat wins dismissal of antitrust suit.
newsitem.headline: Comsat wins dismissal of antitrust suit.

text.p: A federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit accusing Communications Satellite Corp (Comsat) of engaging in anti-competitive practices in the market for international commercial satellite telecommunications services.
U.S. District Judge John Keenan, in a written decision dated Wednesday, threw out the case filed in Manhattan Federal Court by Alpha Lyracom Space Communications Inc and Pan American Satellite.
This was the third-amended complaint filed by the plaintiffs. The first two versions of the case were filed in 1989.
A district judge dismissed the case in 1990 on grounds that Comsat had immunity from antitrust challenges for its activities with the international consortium known as Intelsat.
Intelsat was created under a 1961 United Nations resolution to operate a global satellite communications system.
Each member nation designates a company to market and operate the Intelsat communications system within its territory.
Comsat was created by 1962 legislation to operate the Intelsat system in the U.S.

In 1991, the Second Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the lower court ruling but remanded the case to give the plaintiffs an opportunity to refile their claims against Comsat in its role as a common carrier with activities outside of Intelsat.
The two firms then appealed to the Supreme Court over the immunity issue, and in 1992 the justices denied the appeal without any comment.

The plaintiffs argued that Comsat and other companies designated by member nations to operate Intelsat systems conspired to prevent Pan American Satellite from gaining access to commercial communications satellite markets by denying or delaying its procurement of operating agreements.
Keenan, in his 160-page ruling, said the plaintiffs had failed to produce evidence of these allegations.
